relations.note: Later traditions make Conchobar Conall’s foster-brother or close kinsman.
Conall serves Conchobar’s court and commands or joins his campaigns.
Welsh forms of Conchobar and Conall appear together in Arthur's catalogue.
They swear that whichever survives will avenge the other before sunset.
Conall competes with Cú Chulainn but fails tests establishing Cú Chulainn’s precedence.
Conall competes with Cú Chulainn and Lóegaire for heroic precedence.
Conall and Cú Chulainn are maternal cousins and foster-brothers.
Conall pursues and kills Cú Chulainn's killers after the hero's death.
Conall guards or attends Cú Chulainn and questions an otherworld messenger.
Later versions say Conall brings Lugaid’s severed head to Emer.
Emer and Conall share a dialogue preserved in Scottish Gaelic tradition.
relations.source: Book of the Dean of Lismore

relations.note: Emer contrasts Conall’s standing with Cú Chulainn’s while asserting precedence.
Conall avenges Cú Chulainn and returns where Emer mourns the body.
Conall kills Ailill partly to avenge Ailill’s killing of Fergus.
Conall and Fergus appear together as violent heroes suffering punishment.
Fergus and Conall appear together among the senior Ulster champions.
Medb acts as an adjudicating queen during the champion’s-portion tests.
Conall obeys Medb’s request to kill Ailill and avenge Fergus.
Medb helps support the aged Conall despite his feud with Connacht.
Conall appears among the Ulster exiles associated with Medb’s host.
Through daughter Deichtine, Conchobar is Cú Chulainn's maternal ancestor.
Conchobar gives the youth arms and his own adequate chariot equipment.
Conchobar supplies the arms and chariot capable of withstanding him.
Through sister Deichtine, Conchobar is Cú Chulainn's maternal uncle.
Cú Chulainn defends Conchobar's province while the Ulaid remain debilitated.
Cú Chulainn defends Conchobar's Ulaid realm during Medb's invasion.

relations.myth: Deirdre and the sons of Uisliu
relations.note: Conchobar claims Deirdre as intended wife and later holds her coercively.

relations.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
relations.note: Conchobar recovers Deirdre by breaking the safe conduct offered to the exiles.
Conchobar procures the exiles’ return under guarantees and arranges their destruction.
Conchobar transfers Deirdre to Éogan, prompting her suicide against a stone.
Conchobar gives captive Deirdre to Eógan, prompting her fatal act.
Conchobar confines Deirdre before her elopement and holds her after Noísiu’s death.
Conchobar prevents Deirdre’s killing, claiming her for his future bed.
Conchobar appears as king and relative within Emer's wooing narrative.
Conchobar presides over or responds to disputes involving Emer’s household.

relations.myth: Betrayal of the sons of Uisliu
relations.note: Conchobar breaks the safe conduct guaranteed by Fergus, driving him into exile.

relations.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
relations.note: Conchobar engineers Fergus’s separation and violates his guarantee by killing the brothers.
The exiled Fergus becomes Conchobar's enemy after the Uisliu betrayal.
Fergus rebels, attacks Emain Macha, and becomes Conchobar’s enemy after the betrayal.
Fergus threatens Conchobar in battle but loyalty and fosterage restrain him from killing him.
Fergus yields the kingship temporarily, but Conchobar retains it permanently.
After losing the throne, Fergus remains in Conchobar’s service for a time.
Their adapted Welsh names appear together in Arthur's catalogue of courtiers.
A later medieval tradition makes Medb Conchobar's former wife.
Medb invades Conchobar's province to seize Donn Cúailnge.
Medb invades Conchobar’s province and wages war against Ulster.
Conchobar rapes Medb after their marriage has failed.
Emer is his wife in the principal canonical tradition.
Emer and Cú Chulainn test one another through reciprocal riddling dialogue.
They exchange learned riddles before he later carries her from Forgall's stronghold.
Emer warns Cú Chulainn that Connla is his son and opposes combat.
Emer rebukes his neglect and confronts his affair with Fand.
Cú Chulainn carries the consenting Emer from her father’s fortress.
Emer recognizes or suspects Connla's identity and urges Cú Chulainn to show restraint.
Emer confronts his affair with Fand; both women ultimately offer to relinquish him.
Emer mourns Cú Chulainn and reproaches those who failed to protect him.
They campaign together, capture Germán, and share a pact of friendship.
The foster-brothers fight over several days while exchanging food and weapons between combats.
The former foster-brothers fight through several escalating days at the ford.
relations.source: Táin Bó Cúailnge, Recensions I and II

relations.myth: Nightly exchanges during the ford combat
relations.note: Ferdiad sends half his food and drink to the wounded Cú Chulainn.
Cú Chulainn kills Ferdiad with the gáe bolga and laments him.
Ferdiad is his former fellow pupil and foster-brother under Scáthach.
Ferdiad and Cú Chulainn are described as foster-brothers or fellow fosterlings.
relations.source: Táin Bó Cúailnge, Recensions I and II

relations.note: Fergus negotiates Cú Chulainn’s terms, warns him, and protects him against unfair opponents.
Fergus is Cú Chulainn’s foster-father and master.
They confront one another, but Fergus withdraws under an earlier reciprocal agreement.
They arrange reciprocal retreats: Cú Chulainn flees first, then Fergus routs Connacht by withdrawing.
Fergus has a mentor or foster relationship with Cú Chulainn.
As foster-father and master, Fergus recounts and interprets the boy’s early achievements.
He bargains with Medb's host for a succession of single combats.
Cú Chulainn delays and attacks Medb's invading army through guerrilla warfare and single combats.
Medb commands the army opposed by Ulster’s principal defender.
Medb offers cattle, land, women, and rewards to halt his attacks.
Cú Chulainn encounters Medb exposed and guards her retreat instead of killing her.
Macpherson coordinates Oisín and Cuchullin within his remodeled Ossianic setting.
Cú Chulainn joins Scáthach’s sons, defeats Aífe’s forces, and secures her submission.
An alternative medieval version makes Scáthach his sexual partner before she prophesies.
The late training romance grants him an ongoing sexual relationship with Scáthach.
Scáthach teaches or supplies him with the deadly gáe bolga.
Scáthach foretells his combats, bloodshed, and ordeals during the cattle raid.
He holds a sword to her breast and compels instruction, Uathach, and prophecy.
After killing Cochar, Cú Chulainn undertakes to lead and champion Scáthach’s host.
Scáthach trains Cú Chulainn in martial arts.
Scáthach teaches him advanced military feats and exclusive use of the gáe bolga.
Deirdre’s party requests Fergus as guarantor, but he fails to accompany them.
Deirdre condemns Fergus for selling his honor for ale.

relations.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
relations.note: Fergus pledges protection to Deirdre and escorts her party from Scotland.
Gráinne is Fionn’s wife before repudiating him and separating.
Gráinne is Finn’s intended bride before fleeing with Diarmuid.
Later variants make Finn take, win, or marry Gráinne after Diarmuid dies.
Fionn pursues the fugitive couple after Diarmaid violates loyalty to him.
Finn relentlessly pursues Diarmuid after he flees with Gráinne.
Gráinne is Fionn’s intended bride but drugs him and escapes with Diarmaid.
Fionn twice spills healing water while Diarmaid lies mortally wounded.
Finn delays healing the boar-wounded Diarmuid and lets the curative water spill.
Diarmaid serves as an elite warrior under Fionn’s command.
Oisín repeatedly sympathizes with Diarmaid and opposes Fionn’s vindictiveness.
Diarmaid and Oisín are fellow Fenians in joint adventures.
Oisín refuses Gráinne because she has been promised to Fionn.
Oisín accompanies the Fianna pursuing Diarmaid and Gráinne.
Oisín counsels Diarmaid that Gráinne’s binding geis cannot honorably be ignored.
Ferguson's poem has Oisín direct the burial of Oscar's wife Aideen.
Fergus advises Ferdiad against the fatal encounter, but Ferdiad disregards him.
In Ardee folklore, a giant Fear-dhiadh challenges Fionn before Fionn's wife kills him.
Medb uses threatened satire, rewards, Finnabair, and honour to manipulate Ferdiad.
relations.source: Táin Bó Cúailnge, Recensions I and II

relations.note: Medb recruits or coerces Fer Diad with wealth, marriage, threats, and satire.
After Ferdiad's company delivers Germán, Scáthach imposes friendship and concord.
Scáthach is named as Ferdiad's martial instructor and foster-mother.
An alternative tradition names Fer Diad among Scáthach’s Irish warrior pupils.
Fergus guides Medb’s army and advises her about Ulster and Cú Chulainn.
Fergus becomes Medb’s lover during his Connacht exile.
Fergus maintains a sexual relationship with Medb.
Medb entwines herself around Fergus while swimming immediately before his fatal spearing.
Medb restores or facilitates the return of Fergus’s sword.
Medb recruits Fergus, relies on his Ulster knowledge, and appoints him to command.
Oisín is Finn and Sadhbh’s son, warrior, poet, and memorial narrator.
Oisín fights and hunts under Fionn, his leader.
Scáthach foresees Medb’s cattle-raid expedition but never meets her.
Comparativists propose correspondences between Pryderi and the Grail hero Peredur or Percival.
Pryderi and Taliesin are among the seven survivors returning from Ireland.
Taliesin and Pryderi survive Bran’s expedition and journey home together.
Pryderi is named in the otherworld expedition narrated by Taliesin’s voice.
Pwyll is named in the otherworld episode narrated by Taliesin.

god_relations.note: Lug claims divine paternity in one supernatural conception tradition.

god_relations.myth: Lug heals and aids Cú Chulainn
god_relations.note: Lug appears during the campaign to heal or assist his wounded son.
The disguised Morrígan encounters, threatens, and prophetically warns Cú Chulainn.
She attacks as eel, wolf, and heifer; Cú Chulainn wounds each form.
His blessings unknowingly heal her wounds while she appears as an old milkmaid.

god_relations.myth: Manannán separates Fand and Cú Chulainn
god_relations.note: Manannán shakes his cloak between the lovers so they can never meet again.
Rhiannon’s wonder-working birds are demanded, but Culhwch never meets her.
Later Fenian genealogies sometimes name Donn as Diarmaid’s father.

god_relations.myth: Separation of Fand and Cú Chulainn
god_relations.note: Manannán removes Fand and permanently separates her from Emer’s husband.
The Dagda supplies supernatural labor enabling Óengus to obtain Étaín for Midir.
Modern scholars propose Fergus as a euhemerized deity or epic reflex of the Dagda.
Isolated later material makes the divine Nuada Finn’s ancestor.
Finn encounters the otherworld ruler in developed Fenian narratives.
Developed traditions associate Finn’s encounters with gifts from Manannán.
Bres is one of Medb’s three brothers, the Trí Find Emna.
Medb and Ailill encounter the Morrígan, her magical cow, and prophecy.
Pwyll substitutes for Arawn, defeats his rival, and becomes his enduring ally.
Arawn sends the otherworld pigs that Pryderi later owns.
Pwyll follows Rhiannon's marriage plan and marries her after overcoming Gwawl.
Pryderi is Rhiannon's abducted and eventually restored son.
Pryderi and Rhiannon are magically trapped together and later released.
Pryderi joins Bendigeidfran's Irish expedition and helps carry his severed head.
Pryderi joins the expedition mounted after Branwen's abuse in Ireland.
Manawydan is Pryderi's fellow survivor, friend, guest, and eventual stepfather.
Pryderi offers Manawydan the use of Dyfed and marriage to Rhiannon.
Manawydan coerces Llwyd into releasing the magically imprisoned Pryderi.
Pryderi and Manawydan are jointly associated with the otherworldly Caer Siddi.
god_relations.source: Song before the Sons of Llyr

god_relations.note: Gwydion trades magically counterfeited animals and equipment for Pryderi's pigs.
Gwydion obtains Pryderi's pigs through illusory barter and drives them north.
Pryderi challenges Gwydion to settle their devastating war in single combat.
Gwydion kills Pryderi through martial strength, magic, and enchantment.
Pryderi leads Dyfed against the northern host ruled by Math.

god_relations.myth: Return from Ireland with Bran’s severed head
god_relations.note: Taliesin survives the catastrophe and accompanies Bran’s speaking head to Britain.
Taliesin and the other survivors listen to Rhiannon’s wondrous birds.
Ceridwen swallows Gwion, gestates him, and gives birth to Taliesin.
Taliesin as Gwion exchanges successive animal and vegetal forms while fleeing Ceridwen.
Gwion accidentally receives the wisdom intended to emerge from Ceridwen’s cauldron.
Taliesin invokes Gwydion and claims knowledge predating him.

god_relations.myth: Journey to Lleu and Gwydion’s city
god_relations.note: Taliesin invokes Lleu in magical questions and says he will visit his city.

Achall.myth: Conall brings Erc’s head to Tara
Achall.note: Conall’s delivery of Erc’s head causes Achall to die from grief.

Aebgréine.note: Aebgréine is named as Deirdre and Noísiu’s daughter in later tradition.

Aengus Óg.note: Aengus shelters the fugitives whom Finn pursues and later mourns Diarmuid.

Afagddu.note: After rebirth through Ceridwen, Taliesin is Afagddu’s social half-brother.
Taliesin as Gwion receives the cauldron’s wisdom originally intended for Afagddu.

Afallach.note: Afallach is Owain's maternal grandfather through Modron.

Aichlech mac Duibdrenn.note: Aichlech kills and decapitates Finn at Áth Brea on the Boyne.

Ailill Finn.note: Fergus enters Ailill Finn’s territory under pretext and fights him.
In the older tale complex, Fergus kills Ailill Finn and carries off Flidais.

Ailill mac Mágach.note: Expanded husband lists associate Ailill mac Mágach with Medb.

Ailill mac Máta.note: Ailill receives and supports the aged, debilitated Conall at Cruachu.
Conall kills Ailill with a spear at Medb’s prompting.
Conchobar and Ailill's Connacht party compete for Mac Dathó's hound.
Ailill co-leads the Connacht invasion of Conchobar's Ulster.
Cú Chulainn opposes the invasion jointly led by Ailill and Medb.
Ferdiad is received in Ailill's camp amid proposed rewards and sureties.
Fergus enters Ailill’s household and commands exiles in the Connacht invasion.
Ailill removes Fergus’s sword after finding him with Medb and substitutes wood.
Jealous Ailill engineers Fergus’s death by deceiving Lugaid into spearing him.
Ailill is Medb’s principal husband and co-ruler of Connacht.
Medb and Ailill jointly command the invasion of Ulster.
Scáthach foresees Ailill’s part in the expedition but never meets him.

Aillén mac Midgna.note: Finn resists Aillén’s sleep-music and kills the supernatural attacker.

Ainnle.note: Ainnle supports Deirdre’s elopement, shares her exile, and dies after returning.

Ainnle mac Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Ainnle mac Uisliu.note: Ainnle returns under Conchobar's broken guarantee and is attacked.

Ainnle mac Uisliu.myth: Death of the sons of Uisliu
Ainnle mac Uisliu.note: Ainnle is killed by Conchobar's forces after returning from exile.

Ainnle son of Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Ainnle son of Uisliu.note: Fergus guarantees Ainnle’s safe return but is separated before Ainnle is killed.

Altus.note: Altus brings Conchobar news of Christ's Crucifixion in a variant death account.

Amaethon son of Dôn.note: Ysbaddaden requires Amaethon as ploughman, but his acquisition is not narrated.

Amargen Iarngiunnach.note: Amargen is Conall’s father in the common heroic genealogy.

Amargen Iarngiunnach.myth: Conall returns wounded from Dá Derga’s hostel
Amargen Iarngiunnach.note: Amargen tests Conall’s fidelity after initially reproaching him for surviving Conaire.

Angharad Llaw Eurog.note: Angharad rejects Peredur, then professes love after witnessing his disguised victories.

Anlúan mac Mágach.myth: Champion’s portion at Mac Dá Thó’s feast
Anlúan mac Mágach.note: Conall kills Anlúan and displays his head to answer Cet’s challenge.

Aonghus an Brogha.note: Aonghus is Diarmaid’s supernatural foster-father, not securely his biological father.
Aonghus conceals or carries Gráinne and assists Diarmaid’s escape.
Aonghus mediates the settlement allowing Diarmaid and Gráinne to live together.
Aonghus takes Diarmaid’s body to Brú na Bóinne after his death.

Archgallo.note: Geoffrey's legendary Peredurus and Archgallo are sons of Morvidus.

Ardan mac Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Ardan mac Uisliu.note: Ardan returns under Conchobar's broken guarantee and is attacked.

Ardan mac Uisliu.myth: Death of the sons of Uisliu
Ardan mac Uisliu.note: Ardan is killed by Conchobar's forces after returning from exile.

Ardan son of Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Ardan son of Uisliu.note: Fergus guarantees Ardan’s safe return but is separated before Ardan is killed.

Arddun.note: Later Welsh genealogical tradition makes Arddun Peredur's sister.

Ardán.note: Ardán supports Deirdre’s elopement, shares her exile, and dies after returning.

Art mac Cuinn.note: Gráinne is Art’s granddaughter through her father Cormac.

Arthur.note: As Cnychwr mab Nes, Conchobar is catalogued among Arthur's courtiers.
Arthur is Culhwch’s maternal cousin; the exact genealogical connection is unstated.
Arthur grants Culhwch’s boon, leads the quest, and secures his marriage.
Peredur summons Arthur, whose household helps destroy the Witches of Gloucester.
Pwyll appears in Arthur's courtly orbit, but no shared deed is narrated.
Taliesin is listed as chief bard among Arthur’s courtly retainers.
Taliesin’s poetic voice participates in Arthur’s perilous otherworld expedition.

Athirne.note: Conchobar leads the Ulaid to protect or recover cattle for Athirne.

Aífe.note: Conall confronts Aífe’s son after she sends Connla to Ireland.
Cú Chulainn fights and overcomes Scáthach's rival.
He defeats Aífe by falsely claiming her beloved horses and chariot are falling.
After defeating Aífe, he coerces her into peace terms and sex.
Aífe is named among Ferdiad's foster-mothers and martial instructors.
Scáthach wars against Aífe’s people until Cú Chulainn forces Aífe to submit.
Both women are named as daughters of Ardgeimm and are therefore sisters.
A medieval legal commentary makes Aífe the daughter of Scáthach.

Banw.note: Twrch’s offspring fights Culhwch’s allies and is killed during the hunt.

Bedwyr.note: Bedwyr accompanies Culhwch and helps obtain Mabon, Dillus’s beard, and Diwrnach’s cauldron.

Benandonner.note: Giant Finn challenges or confronts the Scottish giant across the Causeway.
Finn’s household disguises him as a baby, frightening Benandonner into retreat.

Bennwig.note: Twrch’s offspring fights Culhwch’s allies and is killed during the hunt.

Black Oppressor.note: The one-eyed host tells Peredur of the monster that took his eye.

Black Witch, daughter of the White Witch.note: Her blood is demanded for Ysbaddaden’s shaving; no completed encounter survives.

Blackbird of Cilgwri.note: Culhwch’s search-party consults the ancient blackbird while seeking Mabon.

Blaí Derg.note: Learned tradition alternatively names Blaí Derg as Oisín's mother.

Bláthnat.note: Bláthnat assists Cú Chulainn's attack by betraying Cú Roí and giving a signal.

Bodb Derg.note: Some later genealogies make Bodb Derg Oisín's maternal grandfather through Sadhbh.

Bodhmall.note: Bodhmall fosters the hidden child Finn and is sometimes a druidess.

Borrach mac Annti.note: Borrach detains Fergus at a feast, undermining protection promised to Deirdre’s party.

Borrach son of Annti.note: Borrach’s invitation activates Fergus’s prohibition and separates him from the returning exiles.

Bran.note: Finn’s supernatural hound recognizes Sadhbh’s humanity and hunts beside him.

Bricriu.note: Bricriu separately promises Conall and two rivals the champion’s portion.
Bricriu provokes discord and contests intended to determine Cú Chulainn's heroic precedence.
Bricriu manipulates Emer by privately declaring her Ulster’s foremost woman.

Bricriu Nemthenga.note: Bricriu threatens and manipulates Conchobar's court into attending his divisive feast.

Bricriu mac Carbada.note: Fergus injures Bricriu with a chessman after Bricriu insults him.
Bricriu manipulates Fergus’s desire and helps provoke the expanded Flidais conflict.

Buinne.note: Buinne initially protects Deirdre’s party but is bribed or detached from duty.

Buinne Ruad.note: The expanded Deirdre narrative identifies Buinne Ruad as Fergus’s son.

Buinne Ruad.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Buinne Ruad.note: Fergus delegates protection of the sons of Uisliu to Buinne, who later defects.

Bélchú of Breifne.myth: Conall lies wounded after killing Cet
Bélchú of Breifne.note: Bélchú carries the wounded Conall home, intending a later honourable combat.
Conall exchanges beds with Bélchú, causing Bélchú’s sons to kill him.

Bélchú’s three sons.note: Conall switches beds so the sons inadvertently kill their own father.
Conall kills and beheads all three sons after their failed murder plot.

Cai.note: Cai accompanies the quest and obtains several necessities for Culhwch’s marriage.

Cai fab Cynyr.note: Peredur defeats and humiliates Cai for striking the dwarfs.

Cailitín.myth: Combat with Cailitín and his sons
Cailitín.note: Cú Chulainn kills Cailitín and his sons during or around the Táin tradition.

Cailitín's children.note: Cailitín's magically trained surviving children help engineer the fatal coalition and circumstances.

Cairbre.note: Later genealogical arrangements make Cairbre Fergus’s brother or half-brother.

Cairbre Lifechair.note: Finn’s Fianna oppose Cairbre, although Oscar is his direct final opponent.

Cairpre Nia Fer.note: Cairpre is Conchobar's son-in-law through Fedelm Noíchrothach.
Cairpre becomes Conchobar's enemy during the retaliatory Ros na Ríg campaign.

Calatín Dána.note: Fergus objects when Calatín and his descendants are counted as one opponent.
Medb’s host recruits Calatín and his sons against Cú Chulainn.

Cat.note: The late training romance identifies Cat as Scáthach’s son.
Cat is Scáthach’s champion before Cú Chulainn kills and beheads him.

Cathbad.note: The short conception recension names Cathbad as Conchobar's father.
Cathbad explains the cosmic disturbance and Christ's Crucifixion to Conchobar.
Cathbad declares the boy's heroic name after the hound's death.

Cathbad.myth: Prophecy of brief life and fame
Cathbad.note: Cathbad prophesies that taking arms brings lasting fame but a short life.
Cathbad names Deirdre and predicts her beauty and Ulster’s resulting disasters.
Later genealogical arrangements make Cathbad Fergus’s brother or kinsman.

Caw of Prydain/Pictland.note: Caw holds the boar’s tusk and shaves Ysbaddaden, enabling Culhwch’s marriage.

Caílte mac Rónáin.note: Caílte defeats Gráinne’s delaying stratagem by gathering the animals for Fionn.
Caílte is among the fénnidi who sympathize with Diarmaid.
Finn’s nephew or kinsman is his swift companion and later narrator.
Caílte is Oisín's fellow surviving Fenian and traveling companion.

Celtchar mac Uthechair.note: Celtchar sits near Conchobar and serves him as a champion.

Cet mac Mágach.note: Conall’s maternal uncle Cet crushes or bends his neck beneath his heel.

Cet mac Mágach.myth: Champion’s portion at Mac Dá Thó’s feast
Cet mac Mágach.note: Conall defeats Cet’s claim by producing the severed head of Anlúan.

Cet mac Mágach.myth: Conall tracks Cet through the snow
Cet mac Mágach.note: Conall fights and kills Cet after an Ulster raid.
Cet steals Mesgegra's brain-ball from Conchobar's royal centre at Emain.
Cet strikes Conchobar in the head with Mesgegra's brain-ball.

Cett.note: Cett is identified as one of Scáthach’s two sons.
Scáthach teaches Cett when Cú Chulainn approaches and threatens her.
Her son joins Cú Chulainn in combat against Aífe’s warriors.

Cet’s son.myth: Conall’s last stand at the ford
Cet’s son.note: Cet’s son leads the pursuers who kill and behead the fleeing Conall.

Christ.note: Taliesin’s legendary persona claims presence or service beside Christ.

Ciar.note: Genealogical tradition makes Ciar Fergus’s son and the Cíarraige’s ancestor.

Cigfa ferch Gwyn Glohoyw.note: Cigfa is Pryderi's wife and shares the emptied Dyfed with him.

Cilydd son of Celyddon.note: Cilydd is Culhwch’s father and advises him to seek Arthur.

Clothru.note: An inconsistent learned notice names Clothru as mother of Conchobar's son.
Clothru is Medb’s sister and predecessor at Cruachan.
Medb kills Clothru and subsequently takes Connacht.

Cochar.note: Cochar serves as Scáthach’s household champion until Cú Chulainn kills him.

Conaire Mór.note: Conall serves as Conaire’s guest and defender but cannot prevent his death.
Étaín’s descendants establish the supernatural ancestry of Conaire Mór.

Conall Casdamail.note: One political pedigree makes Conall Casdamail Conall’s seventh-generation descendant.

Condere mac Echach.note: Conall accepts Connla’s challenge after Condere fails to turn him away.

Conmac.note: Genealogical tradition makes Conmac Fergus’s son and the Conmaicne’s ancestor.

Conn Cétchathach.note: Gráinne is named as a remote descendant of Conn.
Comparative scholarship proposes a structural correspondence between Pwyll and Conn Cétchathach.

Connla.note: Conall challenges Connla, who throws him down and binds him.
Conchobar joins the Ulster confrontation culminating in Connla's fatal combat.
Connla is Cú Chulainn's son by Aífe.
Cú Chulainn unknowingly kills Connla with the gáe bolga before recognizing him.
Emer recognizes Connla as her husband’s son and pleads against his killing.
Scáthach withholds gáe bolga instruction from Connla, enabling Cú Chulainn’s fatal advantage.

Conán Cualann.note: Expanded husband lists associate Conán with Medb.

Conán mac Morna.note: Conán participates in pursuit traditions, though his allegiance varies between witnesses.
Conán is Oisín's fellow Fenian and companion in adventures.

Cormac Con Loinges.note: Cormac and Conall share Ulaid allegiance and scenes without a major paired episode.
Cormac is Conchobar's son and intended successor.

Cormac Con Loinges.myth: Betrayal of the sons of Uisliu
Cormac Con Loinges.note: Conchobar's broken guarantee drives his son Cormac into Connacht exile.

Cormac Cond Longas.note: Fergus is Cormac’s foster-father rather than his biological father.
Cormac accompanies his foster-father Fergus into exile and the Connacht alliance.
Cormac restrains or mediates Fergus’s violence against Conchobar.

Cormac Cond Longas.myth: Exile of the sons of Uisliu
Cormac Cond Longas.note: Medb and Ailill shelter the exiled Cormac at Cruachan.
Cormac serves in Medb’s host but nearly turns against her.

Cormac mac Airt.note: Gráinne is consistently identified as Cormac’s daughter.
Cormac joins the pursuit or political opposition against the couple.
Cormac grants Ceis Corainn to Diarmaid as Gráinne’s dowry.

Cormac mac Conchobuir.note: Cormac serves as requested guarantor and joins the subsequent exile.

Creirwy.note: After rebirth through Ceridwen, Taliesin is Creirwy’s social half-brother.

Crunnchu.note: Crunnchu's boast before Conchobar provokes the forced race of his pregnant wife.

Culann.note: Conchobar attends Culann's feast, which Sétanta follows before killing the hound.
After killing Culann's guard dog, Sétanta promises to replace and serve as its defender.

Cumall.note: Finn is Cumall’s son and inherits his feud and leadership claim.
Oisín is Cumall's grandson through Fionn mac Cumhaill.

Custennin.note: Custennin is Culhwch’s maternal uncle or close maternal kinsman.
Custennin receives Culhwch’s ring and shelters his party.

Cynddylig Cyfarwydd.note: Arthur appoints Cynddylig as guide for Culhwch’s initial party.

Cynfelyn Drwsgl.note: Peredur and Cynfelyn ride Corvan to observe Gwenddolau's host.

Cú Roí mac Dáire.note: Cú Roí tests the rival champions belonging to Conchobar's court.
Their adapted Welsh names appear together in Arthur's catalogue of courtiers.
Cú Roí tests the champions and declares Cú Chulainn supreme after he submits his neck.
Cú Chulainn and Cú Roí compete over captives or treasure, including Bláthnat.
Cú Roí defeats or humiliates Cú Chulainn in divergent versions.
Cú Chulainn's party kills Cú Roí after Bláthnat betrays and signals against him.

Cú Roí mac Dáiri.note: Cú Roí judges or engineers the ordeal that Conall refuses or fails.
Fergus and Cú Roí are co-listed among Irish figures at Arthur’s court.

Cúar.note: Cúar is identified as one of Scáthach’s two sons.
Scáthach teaches Cúar when Cú Chulainn approaches and threatens her.
Her son joins Cú Chulainn in combat against Aífe’s warriors.

Cúr mac Da Lóth.note: Medb summons Cúr to her tent and sends him against Cú Chulainn.

Cúscraid Mend Macha.note: Cúscraid is Conchobar's son and eventual successor in some king-lists.

Dam Dreimed.note: Ferdiad kills Dam Dreimed during the expedition.

Dam Dílend.note: Ferdiad kills Dam Dílend during the expedition.

Damán.note: Ferdiad is consistently named as the son of Damán.
Damán.source: Táin Bó Cúailnge, Recensions I and II

Deichtine.note: One conception recension makes Deichtine Conchobar's daughter.
A competing conception recension makes Deichtine Conchobar's sister.
Deichtine accompanies Conchobar during the expedition framing Cú Chulainn's conception.
Deichtine is his mother in both conflicting conception sequences.

Deirg Drúchtach.note: Conall’s horse tears Lugaid’s side, enabling Conall’s victory.

Diarmaid and Gráinne’s children.note: The settled couple have children, whose names and number vary by recension.

Diarmaid’s unnamed or variably named boa.note: A later account makes Diarmaid kin to the being transformed into the boar.

Dillus Farchog.note: Dillus’s living beard is taken by Cai and Bedwyr for Culhwch’s quest.

Diorraing mac Dobair Uí Bhaoiscne.note: Diorraing recommends Gráinne to Fionn as a suitable wife.

Diwrnach Wyddel.note: Culhwch’s allies seize Diwrnach’s cauldron after he refuses to surrender it.

Donn Cuailnge.note: Scáthach prophetically foresees the Brown Bull’s final contest.

Donn Cúailnge.note: The invasion of Conchobar's province is undertaken to seize this supernatural bull.
Cú Chulainn defends the territory and herd invaded because of the supernatural bull.
Medb invades Ulster to seize the bull and has it driven into camp.

Dub Sainglend.note: Dub Sainglend is Cú Chulainn's other principal chariot-horse.

Dubthach Doéltenga.note: Dubthach serves as requested guarantor and retaliates after the pledge is broken.

Dubthach Dóeltenga.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Dubthach Dóeltenga.note: Conchobar violates Dubthach's guarantee, causing him to repudiate the king.
Dubthach is Fergus’s co-guarantor, fellow rebel, exile, and Connacht ally.
Dubthach accompanies Fergus into Ailill Finn’s territory during the Flidais raid.

Duibne.note: Diarmaid’s designation Ua Duibne implies descent from this eponymous ancestor.

Dunawd Fyr.note: Peredur and Dunawd ride Corvan to observe Gwenddolau's host.

Dáire.note: Ferdiad's full patronymic identifies Dáire as his paternal grandfather.

Dáire Donn.note: Finn leads Ireland’s defenders against Dáire Donn’s invading forces.

Dáire mac Fiachna.note: Medb negotiates to borrow Dáire’s bull before the agreement collapses.
Medb attacks after Dáire withdraws permission to lend the bull.

Eagle of Gwernabwy.note: The eagle directs Culhwch’s search-party toward the salmon who knows Mabon’s prison.

Efnisien.note: Pryderi and Efnisien belong to the British expedition, without an individual exchange.

Efrawg.note: The romance hero is the youngest son of Efrawg, earl of the North.

Eibhir.note: Later sources name Eibhir or Eimhear as Oisín's wife or partner.

Eithne Aittencháithrech.note: Genealogical compilations list Eithne as a spouse or variant of Mugain.

Eithne Ingubai.note: Eithne occupies the wife-role assigned to Emer in another textual layer.

Eithne Uathach.note: Eithne is named as Medb’s sister.

Elidurus.note: Geoffrey's legendary Peredurus and Elidurus are brothers.
Peredurus and Ingenius depose and imprison their brother Elidurus.

Eliffer Gosgorddfawr.note: The northern Peredur is named as Eliffer's son.

Eochaid Dála.note: Eochaid protects Medb and the retreating Connachta.
Eochaid marries Medb and becomes king through their union.

Eochaid Feidlech.note: Medieval genealogies name Eochaid as Medb’s father.
Eochaid responds to Conchobar’s assault on Medb and supports her authority.

Eochaid Sálbuide.note: Fergus succeeds Eochaid as king after Eochaid’s death.

Eochu Sálbuide.note: Eochu Sálbuide is Conchobar's maternal grandfather through Ness.

Erc.note: Conall kills and beheads Erc as one of Cú Chulainn’s killers.

Erc mac Cairpri.note: Erc participates in the enemy coalition that fights and kills Cú Chulainn.

Esa.note: A learned place-lore variant names Esa as Étaín’s daughter.

Etarcomol.note: Etarcomol provokes him despite Cú Chulainn's efforts to avoid combat.
Cú Chulainn kills Fergus's young companion after the provocation.

Etarcumul.note: Fergus warns Etarcumul against arrogance and attempts to mediate his encounter with Cú Chulainn.

Ethne Ingubai.note: One transmitted strand names Ethne Ingubai, rather than Emer, as his wife.

Evirallin.note: Macpherson names Evirallin as Oisín's partner in his remodeled genealogy.

Eógan mac Durthacht.myth: Death of the sons of Uisliu
Eógan mac Durthacht.note: Eógan attacks and kills the sons of Uisliu on Conchobar's behalf.

Fachtna Fáthach.note: The expanded conception tradition names Fachtna as Conchobar's biological father.

Fand.note: Cú Chulainn and Fand become lovers before ultimately renouncing their union.
Emer confronts her romantic rival; both women offer to yield Cú Chulainn.

Fedelm.note: Medb questions Fedelm, then rejects her warning of the army’s slaughter.

Fedelm Noíchride.note: Emer competes with Fedelm Noíchride for precedence among Ulster’s women.

Fedelm Noíchrothach.note: Fedelm is Conchobar's daughter in the Ros na Ríg tradition.

Fedlimid mac Daill.note: Fedlimid is Conchobar's storyteller and hosts the gathering where Deirdre is born.

Feidlimid mac Daill.note: Deirdre is born in the household of her father, Conchobar’s storyteller.

Fer Báeth.note: Fer Báeth and Ferdiad campaign together as companions against Germán.

Fer Doirich.note: Sadhbh’s supernatural persecutor reclaims her, separating Finn from his partner.

Fer Démain mac Damáin.note: The late training narrative apparently presents Fer Démain as another son of Damán.
Fer Démain and Ferdiad train together and remain for an additional year.

Fergus Foga.note: Genealogical schemes sometimes connect or confuse him with Fergus mac Róich.

Fergus Fínbél.note: Some genealogies, lays, and romances name Fergus among Finn’s children.

Fergus mac Lua.note: Fergus mac Lua and Ferdiad appear together as pupils in the late narrative.

Fergus mac Léti.note: Modern comparativists treated the two Ulster kings as doubles of one mythic type.

Fiachra.note: Keating identifies the escort sent by Fergus as Fergus’s son.

Fiachu.note: Fiachu appears among Conchobar's sons in the Deirdre cycle.

Fiachu mac Fir Aba.note: Fergus sends Fiachu to observe or aid Cú Chulainn against Calatín’s family.

Fiachu mac Fir Fhebe.note: Fiachu accompanies the exiles in Medb’s host but secretly assists Cú Chulainn.

Fial.note: Fial is Emer’s sister or foster-sister, depending on the recension.

Find mac Rossa.note: Conchobar fights Find among his Leinster and Gailióin opponents.

Findabair.note: Findabair is the daughter of Medb and Ailill.
Medb repeatedly uses Findabair’s prospective marriage to recruit warriors.

Findmór.note: Medb kills Findmór before sacking Dún Sobairche.

Finnabair.note: Finnabair serves Ferdiad drink, kisses him, and publicly names him her chosen lover.

Finnbennach.note: The bull leaves Medb’s herd for Ailill’s, creating the disputed inequality.

Finnbennach Aí.note: Scáthach prophetically foresees the White-horned Bull’s final contest.

Finnchóem.note: Finnchóem is Conall’s mother in the common heroic genealogy.

Finnéces.note: The poet teaches Finn, who accidentally gains the salmon’s destined wisdom.

Flidais.note: Flidais desires and aids Fergus, then joins him after Ailill Finn’s defeat.
Medb joins the campaign that brings Flidais and her cattle from Mayo.

Folloman.note: Folloman is named as Conchobar's son.
Folloman assumes military command during the invasion of Ulster.

Forgall Monach.myth: Forgall sends him to foreign training
Forgall Monach.note: Forgall directs him toward dangerous overseas training, hoping he will die.
Cú Chulainn storms Forgall's stronghold and kills defenders while carrying off Emer.
Emer is Forgall’s daughter; he opposes her marriage to Cú Chulainn.

Fothad Airgdech.note: Oisín's attributed poem identifies and commemorates Fothad's grave.
Fothad Airgdech.source: Ogum i llia lia uas lecht

Fráech.myth: Recovery expedition to the foreign fort
Fráech.note: Conall accompanies Fráech, sacks the fort, and recovers his family and cattle.
Medb and Ailill test Fráech and expose him to a water monster.
Fráech later joins Medb and Ailill’s military expedition.
A disputed ogham reading may call Fráech the son of Medb.

Fráech Fáil mac Fidach.note: Fráech Fáil and Ferdiad appear together as pupils in the late narrative.

Fráech’s three sons.myth: Recovery expedition to the foreign fort
Fráech’s three sons.note: Conall and Fráech rescue Fráech’s three captive sons.

Fráech’s wife.myth: Recovery expedition to the foreign fort
Fráech’s wife.note: Conall and Fráech rescue Fráech’s captive wife.

Fuamnach.note: Fuamnach changes Étaín through water and worm forms into a beautiful winged insect.

Fuamnach.myth: Étaín driven away by magical winds
Fuamnach.note: Fuamnach twice uses supernatural wind to drive Étaín from her protectors.

Furbaide Ferbend.note: Later genealogical tradition identifies Furbaide as Conchobar's son.
Furbaide is Medb’s nephew through Clothru in one genealogy.
Furbaide is Medb’s nephew through Eithne in competing genealogies.

Furbaide Ferbend.myth: Death of Medb at Inis Clothrann
Furbaide Ferbend.note: Furbaide kills Medb with hard cheese fired from a sling.

Fíachu mac Fergusa.note: Fíachu accompanies Deirdre’s party and dies shielding Noísiu during the attack.

Fíamain mac Fora.note: He is named among Scáthach’s pupils in the redactor’s variant list.

Fíamain mac Forai.note: A variant lists Fíamain and Ferdiad together as fellow pupils.

Fúad mac Forníuil.note: Ferdiad kills Fúad during the retrospective expedition against Germán.

Gann.note: Gann is included among Conchobar's sons in later lists.

Gaíar.note: Gaíar is named as Deirdre and Noísiu’s son in later tradition.

Gerg son of Illand.note: A death-tale notice names Gerg among warriors killed by Fergus.

Germán Garbglas.note: Ferdiad and his companions capture Germán alive and deliver him to Scáthach.

Gilfaethwy.note: Pryderi and Gilfaethwy are fellow survivors of the Irish expedition.

Gilfaethwy fab Dôn.note: Gilfaethwy accompanies Gwydion during the deception that deprives Pryderi of his pigs.
Gilfaethwy joins the northern side in the war provoked against Pryderi.

Glaisne.note: Glaisne is included among Conchobar's sons in later lists.

Glas mac Delga.note: Glas joins the poison-bearing force recruited against Cú Chulainn.

Glewlwyd Gafaelfawr.note: Glewlwyd initially denies Culhwch entry, then announces him to Arthur.

Gofannon son of Dôn.note: Ysbaddaden requires Gofannon as smith, but his acquisition is not narrated.

Goleuddydd daughter of Anlawdd.note: Goleuddydd is Culhwch’s mother and gives birth beside a swine-run.

Goll mac Morna.note: Goll belongs to the pursuing company but sometimes restrains Fionn’s excesses.

Goll mac Morna.myth: Clann Baiscne and Clann Morna feud
Goll mac Morna.note: Cumall’s killer becomes Finn’s hereditary rival and repeatedly quarrels with him.
Despite their feud, Goll later serves under Finn.
Finn and Goll sometimes reconcile and act within the same warrior-band.

Gorbonianus.note: Geoffrey's legendary Peredurus and Gorbonianus are sons of Morvidus.

Goreu son of Custennin.note: Goreu kills Ysbaddaden, removing the final obstacle to Culhwch’s marriage.

Gruddieu.note: Pryderi and Gruddieu are fellow survivors of the Irish expedition.

Grugyn Gwrych Ereint.note: Twrch’s son rejects Arthur’s demand and fights the host serving Culhwch’s quest.

Gwalchmai fab Gwyar.note: Gwalchmai is among the three knights encountered during Peredur's youth.
Gwalchmai quests beside Peredur and joins the final family vengeance.

Gwalchmai son of Gwyar.note: Arthur appoints Gwalchmai as Culhwch’s companion in the search for Olwen.

Gwawl fab Clud.note: Pwyll temporarily loses Rhiannon to Gwawl through a rash promise.
Pwyll tricks Gwawl into an inexhaustible bag and forces him to renounce Rhiannon.
Pwyll's followers beat and humiliate the bagged Gwawl without killing him.

Gweir.myth: Gweir imprisoned in an otherworld fort
Gweir.note: Taliesin’s poem recounts Gweir’s imprisonment during the Annwfn narrative.

Gweir ap Gwystyl.note: Gweir is imprisoned through the uncertain ebostol of Pwyll and Pryderi.

Gweir fab Gwystyl.note: Gweir or Geneir is the third knight encountered near Peredur's forest.

Gwenddolau.note: Peredur belongs to the opposing force against Gwenddolau at Arfderydd.

Gwenhwyfar.note: Culhwch invokes Gwenhwyfar among the guarantors of Arthur’s promised boon.
Peredur avenges the theft of Gwenhwyfar's cup and her public humiliation.

Gwion Bach.note: Gwion is Taliesin’s explicit prenatal identity and transformed continuation.

Gwrgi.note: Brother and fellow son of Eliffer; their deaths are recorded together.
Gwrgi.source: Harley MS 3859 genealogy and Annales Cambriae

Gwrhyr Gwalstawd Ieithoedd.note: Gwrhyr accompanies Culhwch, questions ancient animals, and parleys with Twrch’s family.

Gwyn son of Nudd.note: Gwyn is compelled to join the hunt because his otherworldly fury is indispensable.

Gwys.note: Twrch’s offspring fights Culhwch’s allies and is killed during the hunt.

Hafgan.note: Pwyll, disguised as Arawn, strikes Hafgan once and refuses a restorative second blow.

Harpin of the Mountain.myth: Rescue from Harpin of the Mountain
Harpin of the Mountain.note: Yvain defeats the giant to rescue captives and aid Gawain's relatives.

Heilyn.note: Pryderi and Heilyn are fellow survivors of the Irish expedition.

Hyfaidd Hen.note: Pwyll is entertained at Hyfaidd's court and marries his daughter Rhiannon there.

Iarnan.note: Oisín and other leading Fenians confront the hostile supernatural Iarnan.

Illann Finn.note: The expanded Deirdre narrative identifies Illann Finn as Fergus’s son.

Illann Finn.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Illann Finn.note: Fergus delegates protection of the sons of Uisliu to Illann, who dies defending them.

Illann Fionn.note: Illann fights as a protector of Deirdre and the returning exiles.

Ingenius.note: Geoffrey's legendary Peredurus and Ingenius are brothers.
Peredurus joins Ingenius in deposing Elidurus and dividing Britain.

Irél.note: Irél is named as Conall’s son in some genealogical sources.

Jesus Christ.note: Conchobar and Christ are made same-night counterparts, though not always contemporaries.
Conchobar believes in Christ and declares he would have fought Christ's killers.

Labraid Luathlám ar Claideb.note: Cú Chulainn gives Labraid military assistance against his enemies.

Leborcham.note: Leborcham serves Conchobar as nurse, satirist, or messenger.
Leborcham identifies Noísiu as the man matching Deirdre’s desired colors.
Leborcham brings Emer news of her husband’s death in Gregory’s synthesis.

Lendabair.note: Emer competes with Lendabair for precedence among Ulster’s heroic wives.

Liath Luachra.note: Liath Luachra fosters and trains Finn while he evades his enemies.

Liath Macha.note: The exceptional chariot-horse carries, mourns, and defends Cú Chulainn.

Liath Macha.myth: Death of the Grey of Macha
Liath Macha.note: The horse is killed by an enemy spear during Cú Chulainn's final battle.

Lleminog.note: Lleminog is named in the otherworld expedition context narrated by Taliesin.

Llenlleawg Wyddel.note: Llenlleawg kills Diwrnach and helps secure the cauldron for Culhwch’s wedding.

Llwyd Cil Coed.note: Llwyd enchants Pryderi's land and imprisons him to avenge Gwawl.

Llwydog Gofynniad.note: Twrch’s offspring fights Arthur’s host during Culhwch’s quest and is killed.

Loch Mór mac Egomais.note: A variant lists Loch Mór and Ferdiad together as fellow pupils.

Long mac Emonis.note: Medb recruits Long with clothing, a chariot, hospitality, and Findabair.

Lothar.note: Lothar is one of Medb’s three brothers, the Trí Find Emna.

Luagni of Tara.note: The Luagni are named as the group that kills Finn.

Lug mac Ethnenn.note: Lug appears to Deichtine within an otherworldly episode led by Conchobar.

Lugaid.note: Emer rejects Forgall’s proposed marriage, and Lugaid refuses to take her.
Lugaid and Ferdiad are comrades in the retrospective expedition against Germán.

Lugaid Dalleces.note: Deceived by Ailill, blind Lugaid casts the spear that mortally wounds Fergus.
Lugaid is described as Fergus’s foster-brother and Connacht companion.

Lugaid Riab nDerg.note: Lugaid, Clothru’s son by Medb’s brothers, is Medb’s nephew.

Lugaid mac Con Roí.note: Conall fights one-handed and beheads Lugaid after his horse wounds him.
Lugaid mortally wounds and decapitates Cú Chulainn while avenging Cú Roí.
Emer laments the consequence of Lugaid’s killing of her husband.

Lugaid mac Noís.note: Lugaid enters the narrative at her household, but no direct exchange is preserved.

Láeg mac Riangabra.note: Láeg accompanies the wooing and mediates between Emer and Otherworld parties.
Láeg strips Ferdiad's armour and opens his corpse to recover the weapon.

Lí Ban.note: Lí Ban acts as envoy and mediator, recruiting him for Otherworld warfare.
Lí Ban’s negotiations precipitate Emer’s confrontation with Fand; direct dialogue varies.

Lóch Mór mac Egomais.note: He is named among Scáthach’s pupils in the redactor’s variant list.

Lóch Mór mac Mo Febis.note: Medb secures Lóch’s combat service by promising rewards and Findabair.

Lóch mac Mofemis.note: Cú Chulainn fights Lóch while the Morrígan intervenes in animal forms.
Cú Chulainn kills Lóch in single combat.

Lóeg mac Riangabra.note: Lóeg serves as charioteer, messenger, critic, observer, and battlefield assistant.

Lóegaire Búadach.note: Conall and Lóegaire compete as rival claimants to the champion’s portion.
Lóegaire is a champion at Conchobar's court.
Welsh forms of Conchobar and Lóegaire appear together in Arthur's catalogue.
Lóegaire rivals Cú Chulainn for the champion's portion.
Emer’s claims for Cú Chulainn oppose the household claims of Lóegaire.
Fergus and Lóegaire participate together in Ulster’s heroic precedence traditions.
Fergus and Lóegaire are both included in the Welsh Arthurian court-list.

Lóit Mór mac Mogh Feibis.note: Lóit Mór and Ferdiad appear together as pupils in the late narrative.

Mabon ap Modron.note: Modern comparativists identify Pryderi with Mabon or Maponos from shared narrative motifs.

Mabon son of Modron.note: Culhwch’s allies free Mabon so he can serve as an indispensable hunter.
Mabon hunts Twrch for Culhwch’s quest and takes the razor.

Mac Cécht.note: Both defend Conaire while Mac Cécht seeks water and Conall guards him.

Mac Dathó.note: Mac Dathó promises his celebrated hound to Conchobar and Connacht simultaneously.

Mac Lugach.note: Mac Lugach appears as Oisín's fellow warrior.

Mac Lughach.note: Mac Lughach appears among the fían during the narrative.

Mac Roth.note: Mac Roth serves as Medb’s herald, scout, negotiator, and army reporter.

Macha.note: Conchobar forces pregnant Macha to race his horses; she curses the Ulaid.
Macha's curse disables Conchobar's adult warriors during their greatest danger.
Her curse incapacitates the other Ulaid, indirectly forcing his solitary defence.

Maine Andóe.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Athramail.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Cotagaib Uile.note: Maine Cotagaib Uile is Medb’s son.
He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Mingor.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Máthramail.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Móepirt.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Mórgor.note: He leads troops in Medb’s army.

Maine Rough-hand.note: Maine kills Deirdre’s partner and his brothers in the later recension.

Manannán mac Athgno.note: Manannán fosters Deirdre’s children after their parents’ deaths and returns Gaíar to Ulster.

Manawydan fab Llŷr.note: Taliesin and Manawydan survive the Irish catastrophe and return together.

Matholwch.note: Pryderi serves on the opposing British side against the Irish king.

Medb Lethderg.note: Modern scholarship reconstructs the two medieval Medbs as one sovereignty figure.

Menw son of Teirgwaedd.note: Menw accompanies Culhwch, wounds Ysbaddaden, and scouts Twrch in bird form.

Mes Gedra.note: Conall binds one arm, kills Mes Gedra, and takes his head and brain.

Mesgegra.note: Mesgegra's preserved brain becomes the weapon whose wound ultimately kills Conchobar.

Mess Búachalla.note: In the Tochmarc genealogy, Mess Búachalla is Étaín’s granddaughter.
Compressed recensions make Mess Búachalla a daughter of Étaín.

Midir.note: Midir desires and marries the first Étaín after bride-service secures her.
Midir recognizes, shelters, and cherishes Étaín in her winged insect form.
Midir approaches Étaín disguised as Ailill before revealing his identity.
After winning access through a wager, Midir carries Étaín from Tara.

Modron.note: Modron is named as the bereaved mother of Mabon, whom Culhwch’s allies rescue.
Welsh tradition names Modron daughter of Afallach as Owain's mother.

Mongán mac Fiachna.note: One early account represents Mongán as Finn reborn or remembering Finn’s life.

Morgan le Fay.note: Later Arthurian genealogies make Morgan Owain's mother instead of Modron.
Morgan's magical ointment, administered by an attendant, cures Yvain's madness.

Morvidus.note: Geoffrey's legendary King Peredurus is a son of Morvidus.

Mugain Aitencaithrech.note: Mugain is prominently presented as Conchobar's queen.

Muirgen mac Sencháin.note: Fergus’s ghost recites the recovered Táin to Muirgen at his grave.

Muirne.note: Muirne bears Finn and protects him after Cumall’s death.

Myrddin.note: Geoffrey makes Merlin fight alongside Peredurus against Gwenddolau.
Later writers align or identify the two prophetic bards without secure early support.

Nad Crantail.myth: Combat after obtaining a false beard
Nad Crantail.note: Nad Crantail returns to fight after Cú Chulainn answers his mockery with a false beard.
Cú Chulainn kills the returning champion.

Naoise mac Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Naoise mac Uisliu.note: Conchobar offers safe conduct, then has his rival for Deirdre attacked.

Naoise mac Uisliu.myth: Death of the sons of Uisliu
Naoise mac Uisliu.note: Naoise is killed by forces acting for Conchobar after returning from exile.

Naoise son of Uisliu.myth: Return of the sons of Uisliu
Naoise son of Uisliu.note: Fergus gives Naoise safe-conduct from Scotland, but Conchobar violates the guarantee.

Nath Crantail.note: Medb sends her household champion Nath Crantail against Cú Chulainn.

Nera.note: Nera serves Medb’s court and returns with an Otherworld warning.

Ness.note: Ness is consistently Conchobar's mother across competing conception traditions.
Ness bargains for Conchobar to hold Fergus's kingship for one year.

Nessa.note: Nessa conditions union with Fergus on her son holding the kingship temporarily.

Niamh Chinn Óir.note: Niamh becomes Oisín's lover and otherworld partner.
Niamh Chinn Óir.source: Laoidh Oisín ar Thír na nÓg

Niamh Chinn Óir.note: Niamh guides Oisín overseas to the otherworld.
Niamh Chinn Óir.source: Laoidh Oisín ar Thír na nÓg

Niamh Chinn Óir.myth: Oisín's return from Tír na nÓg
Niamh Chinn Óir.note: Niamh lends Oisín the return-horse and warns him against touching Ireland.
Niamh Chinn Óir.source: Laoidh Oisín ar Thír na nÓg

Nisien.note: Pryderi and Nisien accompany Bendigeidfran, but share no individual exchange.

Noísi mac Uisliu.note: The redactor reports another tradition counting Noísi among Scáthach’s pupils.

Noísiu.note: Deirdre chooses Noísiu, compels his acceptance, and lives with him in exile.

Nuadu Necht.note: Learned genealogies place Finn within Nuadu Necht’s Leinster lineage.

Náisi.note: The late romantic redaction makes Conall an instructor of Náisi and his brothers.

Náisi mac Uisnig.note: A variant lists Náisi and Ferdiad together among Scáthach's pupils.

Nár.note: Nár is one of Medb’s three brothers, the Trí Find Emna.

Olwen.note: Olwen is Culhwch’s predestined beloved and eventual bride.
Olwen reciprocates Culhwch’s love and advises him to petition her father publicly.

Oscar.note: Oscar, Oisín’s son and a leading Fianna champion, is Finn’s grandson.
Oscar fights as a leading champion under Finn’s command.
Oscar is consistently identified as Oisín's son.

Oscar.myth: Wars and hunts of the Fianna
Oscar.note: Oscar is Oisín's fellow Fenian warrior.
Oisín mourns Oscar after his mortal wounding at Gabair.

Oscar mac Oisín.note: Oscar supports Diarmaid and threatens Fionn until he fetches healing water.

Owain fab Urien.note: Owain explains knightly arms and equipment to the ignorant Peredur.

Owain's ravens.myth: The ravens retaliate against Arthur's forces
Owain's ravens.note: Owain commands his supernatural war-birds to attack Arthur's men.

Owl of Cwm Cawlwyd.note: Culhwch’s search-party consults the ancient owl while seeking Mabon.

Pendaran Dyfed.note: Pendaran confirms Pryderi's name and receives him for further fostering.
Pryderi keeps Pendaran's seven swine at Glyn Cuch.

Pluto.note: Early modern mythographers classified Pwyll as the Welsh counterpart of Pluto.

Plúr na mBan.note: Some popular variants make Plúr na mBan a child of Oisín and Niamh.

Raige Rosclethan.note: Some genealogies, lays, and romances name Raige among Finn’s children.

Rhydderch Hael.note: Geoffrey makes Rhydderch and Peredurus allies against Gwenddolau.

Roch.note: A learned genealogy makes the otherworld woman Roch Fergus’s mother.

Ros.note: Later textual and genealogical traditions give Ros or Ross Ruad as Fergus’s father.

Ruad.note: Through his mother Roch, Cóir Anmann makes Fergus a grandson of Ruad.

Rudraige.note: Later genealogical narratives place Fergus among Rudraige’s descendants.

Róech.note: The recurrent patronymic names Fergus as Róech or Róich’s son.

Sadhbh.note: Finn spares the transformed woman, who becomes his partner and Oisín’s mother.
Later deer-transformation traditions name Sadhbh as Oisín's mother.

Salmon of Knowledge.note: Finn cooks and tastes the salmon, thereby acquiring supernatural knowledge.

Salmon of Llyn Llyw.note: The salmon reveals Mabon’s prison and carries Cai and Bedwyr there.

Sceólang.note: Finn’s supernatural hound recognizes Sadhbh’s humanity and hunts beside him.

Senach Síaborthe.note: Cú Chulainn slays Labraid's Otherworld enemy during the campaign.

Sencha mac Ailella.note: Sencha counsels Conchobar and recommends precautions against Bricriu's disruptions.
Sencha acts as judge or peacemaker during Emer’s quarrel with rival wives.

Senchán Torpéist.note: Senchán directs the search for the lost epic and sometimes joins the grave encounter.

Serpent of the foreign fort.note: The unnamed serpent enters and leaves Conall’s belt without harming him.

Stag of Rhedynfre.note: Culhwch’s search-party consults the ancient stag while seeking Mabon.

Sualtach.note: Cóir Anmann makes Fergus and Sualtach maternal brothers through Roch.

Sualtaim mac Róich.note: Sualtaim is his mortal and social father after Deichtine's reconception.

Súaltaim mac Róich.note: Conchobar arranges Deichtine's marriage to Súaltaim in one conception recension.

Tadg mac Nuadat.note: Finn is Tadg’s maternal grandson through Muirne.

Tegid Foel.note: Tegid is Ceridwen’s husband and Taliesin’s social father, not a sexual parent.

Teyrnon Twryf Liant.note: Teyrnon returns Pryderi to Pwyll, who promises him maintenance and reward.
Teyrnon finds infant Pryderi, fosters him as Gwri Wallt Euryn, and returns him.

The Addanc.note: Peredur uses a maiden's aid to find and kill the monster.

The Proud Man of the Clearing.note: Peredur defeats him and requires him to restore the maiden's honor.

The Witches of Gloucester.note: Peredur defeats one witch but grants her quarter.
After his victory, the witches train Peredur in arms for three weeks.
Peredur kills a witch, while Arthur's force destroys the remainder.

Tinni mac Conrach.note: Tinni is Medb’s husband and a king of Connacht.

Twrch Llawin.note: Twrch’s offspring fights Culhwch’s allies and is killed during the hunt.

Twrch Trwyth.note: Culhwch’s allies hunt Twrch and seize his grooming implements, but he escapes.

Uaithne Find.note: Uaithne Find is named as Conall’s son in some genealogical sources.

Uathach.note: Uathach is consistently identified as Scáthach’s daughter in the training narrative.
Uathach reveals how Cú Chulainn can overpower her mother and extract three promises.

Ugnach son of Mydno.note: Taliesin and Ugnach exchange statements about their identities and destinations.

Umall.note: Early forms call Finn mac Umaill, preserving an alternative father-name.

Wrnach Gawr.note: Wrnach’s sword is required for Culhwch’s quest; Cai kills Wrnach with it.

Ynawg.note: Pryderi and Ynawg are fellow survivors of the Irish expedition.

Ysbaddaden Pencawr.note: Ysbaddaden attacks Culhwch, who returns the poisoned spear and pierces his eye.
Ysbaddaden imposes proliferating tasks as the price of Culhwch marrying Olwen.

Ysgithyrwyn Pen Baedd.note: Arthur’s host kills Ysgithyrwyn and obtains his tusk for Culhwch’s quest.

sons of Uisliu.myth: Expanded vengeance for the sons of Uisliu
sons of Uisliu.note: The late redaction makes Conall their instructor or avenging associate.

the Fianna.note: Finn commands the mobile warrior-band in hunting, defense, raiding, and supernatural warfare.

the boar of Beann Ghulban.note: Diarmaid fights the magical boar despite his prohibition concerning boar hunting.
Diarmaid kills the boar after his superior weapons are left behind.
The boar mortally wounds Diarmaid by tearing out his entrails.
A venomous bristle from the boar pierces Diarmaid’s foot and kills him.

the druid at Tara.note: The unnamed druid identifies Diarmaid and describes his exceptional attractiveness.

the lion.myth: The lion's battle with the serpent
the lion.note: Yvain chooses to save the lion from a serpent or dragon.

the lion.myth: Adventures of the Knight of the Lion
the lion.note: The grateful lion becomes Yvain's voluntary companion and co-combatant.

the serpent/dragon.myth: The lion's battle with the serpent
the serpent/dragon.note: Yvain kills the serpent or dragon while rescuing the lion.

the two sons of the devil.note: Yvain defeats two demonic opponents guarding an exploitative labor castle.

Éogan mac Durthacht.note: Éogan kills Noísiu; Deirdre hates him and dies rather than be transferred to him.
Later notices state that Fergus killed Éogan, who had participated in Conchobar’s betrayal.

Óengus.note: Óengus woos Étaín for Midir and completes the tasks demanded for her marriage.
Óengus finds the transformed Étaín and protects her in a portable chamber.

Úathach.note: Úathach is named among Ferdiad's foster-mothers and martial instructors.
